name: Build a GPT
strandNote: Optional for every role. Research roles that build or study language models, and anyone who uses them in research.
description: Tokenise text, run and train a tiny GPT in NumPy, then count what scale and hardware cost.

requires.why: Measures a tokeniser in bits per byte and converts a loss between tokens and characters.
Stacks the transformer block built there into a whole model, without reteaching it.
Trains the model with the array autograd built there, adding the GPT's operations.
Steps with Adam and trains through layer norm, both taught in its first two levels.
Reads a power law as a straight line once both axes are logarithms.
Fits a scaling exponent by least squares on the log-log points.
Rounds to bf16 and fp16, extending the float layout and machine epsilon taught there.

lessonNames.l5-the-whole-model: The whole model on one page
lessonNames.l11-short-runs: What a short run tells you

lessonObjectives.l1-text-as-bytes: Encode text as UTF-8 bytes and explain why a tokeniser starts from bytes.
lessonObjectives.l2-merging-pairs: Write the byte-pair encoding training loop and run its first merges by hand.
lessonObjectives.l3-encode-and-decode: Build an encoder and decoder from a list of merges, and measure bytes per token.
lessonObjectives.l4-cleaning-the-corpus: Write exact and near-duplicate filters for a text corpus.
lessonObjectives.l5-the-whole-model: Derive every array shape and the parameter count of a tiny GPT.
lessonObjectives.l6-loading-weights: Write a loader for supplied weights and check it with the loss of an untrained model.
lessonObjectives.l7-next-character: Code the GPT forward pass in NumPy and match reference logits.
lessonObjectives.l8-generating-text: Build a sampler with temperature and top-k for the tiny GPT.
lessonObjectives.l9-the-training-loop: Build the training loop: batches, loss, backward pass and an Adam step.
lessonObjectives.l10-checking-gradients: Check the GPT's gradients against central differences.
lessonObjectives.l11-short-runs: Use short runs to debug training: overfit one batch and sweep the learning rate.
lessonObjectives.l12-beating-the-bigram: Compute held-out loss per character and show the GPT beats the bigram.
lessonObjectives.l13-counting-parameters: Derive the parameter count of a GPT from its width, depth and vocabulary.
lessonObjectives.l14-counting-compute: Derive the 6ND rule for training compute and apply it to real models.
lessonObjectives.l15-power-laws: Fit a power law by least squares in log space and read its exponent.
lessonObjectives.l16-a-fixed-budget: Choose a model size and token count for a fixed compute budget.
lessonObjectives.l17-waiting-for-memory: Compute arithmetic intensity and decide whether an operation is limited by bandwidth or by arithmetic.
lessonObjectives.l18-fewer-bits: Write bf16 rounding and explain where low precision loses information.
lessonObjectives.l19-what-fits: Build a memory budget for training and for inference.
lessonObjectives.l20-the-kv-cache: Code a KV cache for the tiny GPT and compute its size for a large model.
